title: The loan in cumulative dollars
hook: Does a cumulative dollar bill tell a different story than a two-week fee?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish cost disclosure salience from a change in the loan's actual terms.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish cost disclosure salience from a change in the loan's actual terms.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy €400 loan incurs a €60 fee in each of three cycles. What is the cumulative fee? Toy inputs A=[60, 3, 400]; B=[60, 1, 400].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[180, 400, 60], [60, 400, 60]]. Labels: Cumulative fee €, Principal €, Fee/cycle €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Cumulative disclosure adds the fees across cycles without changing the underlying fee schedule. The principal remains a different quantity. Making a total salient is an information change, not an automatic change to the loan’s contractual cost.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Fee/cycle €=60, Cycles=1, Principal €=400. What is Cumulative fee €? Answer: 60.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Fee/cycle €=60, Cycles=1, Principal €=400. What is Cumulative fee €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 60. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Showing payday borrowers the cumulative dollar cost of a loan cut borrowing about 11% (Bertrand & Morse, 2011).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish cost disclosure salience from a change in the loan's actual terms.
